correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, 1<=b<n coprime, periodic telescoping gives prefix-one count v+[j+r>=n] and suffix-one count v+[r>j]. Equality is equivalent to exactly two explicit disjoint intervals of residues r, each with min(j,n-1-j) members. Coprimality makes r and j permutations of residue classes. Hence all quantifiers, boundary cases and the parity-dependent distribution follow. The checker independently tested 1,965 coprime parameter pairs, 105,388 rotations and 6,250,510 individual border decisions; enumeration does not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The mathematical problem is naturally motivated by exact and Abelian border theory for primitive balanced words: measure how border structure changes as a Christoffel word is cut. A complete all-length, all-coprime-slope classification identifies exact individual border sets, gives the slope-invariant full spectrum, and isolates exactly two Abelian-unbordered rotations plus a parity-sharp unique fully bordered rotation. This exact structural invariant is not a renaming, table extension, or routine numerical special case.
